output.name: *Tolkéva* — "the Laden Beak"
output.myth: When Aun cut the string, the sky went up and the sand-eels went down into the cold, and the puffins were left on the cliffs with empty bellies. Tolkéva was the grey one who dove for them every morning. He came back with his beak full, eels laid crossways like a net-line, and said nothing. Harel the Bone Gull watched from the east. Ennu the Kite-Wright had carved it from whalebone the winter the boats stayed on the shingle, and it never once went down. Tavo the Gale saw Tolkéva diving in a storm, laughed, and tore one wing wide, and still he came home. Hesk the Reel counted every eel he carried and never wrote his name down as a debt. Lethún the Held Gull, north-west, with her torn wing, cried for him to rest. When he reached the pole too tired to speak, Aun came down out of the lamps and took the eels from his beak one by one. Tolkéva is up there still, mouth full. If a puffin comes low over the Reach with nothing said, you know it is him.
output.finding: Find Harel, the Bone Gull, and look a fist's width (about 11°) west of it for the grey diver with his beak full.
